who: People who cannot use a pointer at all
takeaways: Everything can be done with a keyboard alone, with no exceptions, and without needing to press keys at a certain speed.
It is Level AAA. At Level A, 2.1.1 makes an exception for tasks where the result depends on the path of movement, such as freehand drawing. 2.1.3 removes that exception.
Developers build keyboard support. Designers decide what the keyboard version of a path-based task looks like, such as placing points, typing coordinates or picking from shapes.
It is worth aiming for in drawing, signing, map and design tools, where whole tasks are otherwise closed to people who cannot use a pointer.
failures: A signature pad that only accepts a drawn signature
A drawing tool with no way to place or move points by keyboard
A map where an area can only be selected by tracing it
check: List every task that depends on drawing, tracing or a freehand path.
For each, design and write down the keyboard way to reach the same result, even if it is slower.
In the build, complete each task without touching the mouse or trackpad.

quiz.question: A contract flow asks people to draw their signature with a mouse or finger. You want to meet 2.1.3. What do you add?
options: An option to type their name and choose a signature style
A larger drawing area so it is easier to sign
A note that keyboard users should contact support to sign
quiz.why: A drawn signature is path-based, so 2.1.1 makes an exception for it, but 2.1.3 does not. Typing the name reaches the same result by keyboard, while a bigger pad or a support route still leaves keyboard users unable to finish on their own.

spec: For each path-based task, specify the keyboard alternative and the keys that drive it.
Show the alternative in the main flow, not only in settings or help.
Note any part where the keyboard result differs from the drawn one, and why that is acceptable.
review: Is there anything here that only a pointer can do?
If this were AA, would we lean on the freehand exception, and do we need to?
Can someone finish the whole flow without ever touching the mouse?
tradeoff: A keyboard version of drawing can take real design and build effort, and few products need AAA across the board. Meet it where drawing is the main way to finish a task, such as signing or marking areas, and accept the 2.1.1 exception for truly artistic tools.
system: Pair every canvas, signature and drawing component with a keyboard alternative in the library, such as typed signatures and point-by-point shape tools.
pitch: If signing our contract needs a mouse, someone who cannot use one cannot become our customer.
